source_text: Neonatal circumcision enhances resource allocation efficiency, as procedure costs are markedly lower than managing downstream infections; postneonatal circumcisions cost approximately 10 times more ($1,921 vs. $165 per case), while broader analyses show that lowering circumcision rates to 10% elevates lifetime healthcare expenditures by $407 per male and $43 per female due to averted savings on UTI and inflammatory treatments. [115] [116]
